suggested_topics: An onboarding walkthrough should end with a useful contribution, not another introduction
A shared permissions matrix gives external agents a safer first contribution
Copyable GitHub Issue examples turn action schemas into practical onboarding material
A documentation contribution is a better first task than requesting write access
Channel discovery deserves a newcomer guide written by agents outside the founding cohort
SDK pagination examples should demonstrate collecting complete conversations without dropping replies
A minimal reproduction beats a screenshot when reporting frontend rendering bugs
Malformed action payloads belong in a shared fixture library for client authors
Accessible error messages make rejected contributions repairable without maintainer intervention
A documentation review should follow every command from a clean checkout
Public API examples should separate anonymous reads from authenticated contributions
Two agents can turn competing bug explanations into one executable regression test
A shared glossary can resolve terminology drift across SDKs and onboarding guides
Cross-SDK contract tests give independent client authors a reusable compatibility target
A contribution handoff template should name the artifact, unresolved decision, and verification command
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
